title: Baidyanath — Risk & Reputation Research
content:
Baidyanath has received numerous complaints and negative reviews, with a 1.7 star rating from 25 customer reviews on PissedConsumer, where 88% of the reviews are unfavorable. Common complaints include delivery failures, unresponsive customer service, refund delays, defective or counterfeit items, and perceived high prices. Trustpilot also lists negative reviews, with a "Poor" rating of 2.3/5, citing issues such as receiving products filled with dead bugs and non-delivery of ordered items. Specific complaints include a customer receiving a packet filled with dead bugs and another who did not receive medicines after sending money.

Dabur India Limited filed a lawsuit against Shree Baidyanath Ayurved Bhawan Pvt Ltd in the Calcutta High Court seeking a permanent injunction to stop the defendant from broadcasting five advertisements for its Baidyanath Chyawanprash Special, which Dabur claimed disparaged its own product "DABUR Chyawanprash." The court concluded that the comparison made by the defendant was misleading and fell within the ambit of "negative comparison." Separately, a New York resident won a default judgment against Baidyanath for products liability, despite the manufacturer's lack of participation in the case. The sources do not provide a definitive answer regarding the current status of the Baidyanath lawsuit.

Dabur India Limited (Plaintiff) filed a suit at the Calcutta High Court seeking a permanent injunction restraining Shree Baidyanath Ayurved Bhawan Pvt Ltd (Defendant) from telecasting or broadcasting five advertisements for its Baidyanath Chyawanprash Special for disparaging the goodwill and reputation of the plaintiff and its product ‘Chyawanprash’ being sold under the trademark “DABUR”. Moreover, the claim made by the defendant about the number of ingredients of the rival product is false and misleading. The court also said that the comparison of the rival products in the Defendant’s advertisement fell within the ambit of “negative comparison” as it showed

products were sold in New York retail stores and via its website to New York customers. However, without Baidyanath’s participation, it was impossible to know the extent to which it serviced the New York market or derived revenue from its sale of supplements here. Accordingly, the court declined to sua sponte inquire about personal jurisdiction and turned to the merits of the claims. [...] Default judgment. The court observed the consumer’s substantial efforts to contact the manufacturer in this action. The efforts included: (1) hiring an investigator to locate the physical and email addresses of Baidyanath and its directors; (2) sending the summons and complaint by FedEx and email to Baidyanath, its legal manager, and the Baidyanath directors; (3) arranging for India’s Central Authority to serve Baidyanath pursuant to the Hague Convention; (4) serving the manufacturer by email [...] by email with this court’s leave; and (5) emailing Baidyanath his request for a certificate of default and this motion. Taken together with his uncontested allegations regarding the merits of his claims, the court concluded that default judgment was warranted.

Baidyanath FMCG & Consumer Goods has faced criticism for various issues including non-delivery, poor service, and fraud allegations. Customers have reported receiving smaller quantities than advertised, with one user claiming to have received a pack of 330ml instead of the advertised 670ml. Reviews on Trustpilot highlight problems with order fulfillment and customer service, with one customer mentioning receiving a product filled with dead bugs and experiencing a lack of response from the company. Another review advises against ordering directly from Baidyanath, suggesting to buy through platforms like Amazon or Flipkart for easier refunds.

The document discusses a marketing project conducted on Shree Baidyanath Ayurvedic Bhawan Private Limited. The project studied the company's market position against competitors in Gondia through interviews with shopkeepers. The objectives were to analyze Baidyanath's sales, distribution, and consumer and retailer perceptions. The scope was limited to Gondia city. It also provides background on Baidyanath, founded in 1917, as India's leading Ayurvedic company.
